Scientists use AI to produce first high-resolution map of global seagrass extent

2026-07-10 Abhishyant Kidangoor (Mongabay) seagrass mapping, AI, satellite imagery, deep learning, marine conservation, Nature
Read the source article

Quick summary

Arizona State University scientists used satellite imagery and a deep-learning AI model to produce the first high-resolution global map of seagrass ecosystems, revealing that 70% of the world's seagrass is concentrated off just five countries' coasts.

Key takeaways

  • The study mapped 148,506 km² of global seagrass cover — an area larger than England — using satellite data and AI
  • A deep-learning model was trained to identify seagrass from satellite images, with ground-truth corroboration from research dives and underwater cameras worldwide
  • 70% of global seagrass cover is concentrated in just five countries, highlighting conservation priority areas
  • The research was published in Nature (July 2026) and covers two mapping periods: 2019-2020 and 2023-2024
  • Mapping seagrass required different techniques than coral reef mapping, prompting the AI-based approach
